# GitPersona v0.2.0 — Security update, one-command install, and a lighter footprint

Released on `2026-10-29`.

> GitPersona gives each directory its own Git identity: commits, pushes, `gh` and `glab` use the account that
> belongs to the folder you are in, in every tool that runs Git, and `gitpersona verify` proves no repository uses
> the wrong one.

## Summary

A security update, and the first release since v0.1.0. It is built with Go 1.26.10, which fixes 46 vulnerabilities
in the Go standard library that the v0.1.0 binaries contained, so everyone should upgrade. It also brings a
one-command installer, signed build provenance for every download, a prompt that starts no process while you stay
in one folder, far fewer questions to GitHub, and changes that can no longer be left half-written. It runs on macOS
and Linux.

## Who this release is for

Everyone running v0.1.0: upgrade. Your configuration stays as it is and there is nothing to run afterwards; terminal
windows you open after upgrading get the faster prompt.

If you have ever:

- watched your prompt lag for a moment each time you pressed Enter in a big repository
- opened the configuration page and waited while it asked GitHub about every account again
- clicked twice on the page, or ran a command while it was open, and wondered which change won
- pressed Ctrl-C while GitPersona was writing your Git config and hoped it was not left half-done

then v0.2.0 makes GitPersona quiet in your shell, light on GitHub's API, and safe to interrupt.

## Before you upgrade

- **Alpine and Arch packages are gone.** If you installed the v0.1.0 `.apk` or `.pkg.tar.zst` package, remove it
  with your package manager, then install with `install.sh` or the `.tar.gz` archive (see "Install"); your
  configuration in `~/.config/gitpersona` is kept. The `.deb` and `.rpm` packages, Homebrew and `go install` are
  unchanged.

## What you can do now

**Run a patched build.** The binaries are built with the newest Go 1.26 patch release, so Go's security fixes reach
you, and CI fails whenever a known vulnerability is reachable from GitPersona's code.

**Install with one command.** `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/weikxs/gitpersona/main/install.sh | sh`
picks the build for your system and CPU, checks it against `checksums.txt`, installs to `~/.local/bin` without
`sudo` and adds it to your `PATH`. Run it again to upgrade.

**Check where a download came from.** `gh attestation verify <file> --repo weikxs/gitpersona` proves a file was
built by this repository's release workflow from the `v0.2.0` tag and not changed afterwards.

**Keep your prompt instant.** The prompt function, the tide item and the Powerlevel10k segment keep their last
answer while you stay in the same folder and repository, so drawing the prompt again starts no process.

**Change things from two places at once.** The configuration page and the command line take turns: a change never
overwrites another, Apply writes exactly what it showed you, and a change that fails or is interrupted puts every
file back.

## What's new

### Lighter and faster

- **Far fewer questions to GitHub.** `gh auth status` checks every signed-in account against the API; its answer is
  now reused for ten minutes across the page and every command, and asked again when you open or reload the page or
  sign in, out or switch accounts with gh. A failed answer is never reused. Nothing about tokens is kept.
- **Faster checks.** `verify` starts about 4 Git processes per repository instead of 8 plus 4 per remote; preview,
  apply and doctor read each Git config file once; the page gathers shells, checks and accounts at the same time.
- **The overview** reuses its last check while nothing changed, checks at most 200 repositories by itself, and offers
  a button to check them all.
- **`gitpersona ui`** stops about ten seconds after its tab is closed (a reload keeps it running).

### Safer changes

- **All or nothing.** A change that cannot write one file puts back every file it already wrote; Ctrl-C waits until
  the files are written, and files reach the disk before they replace the old ones.
- **One change at a time.** Changes take a lock, and an edit stops without writing when `config.toml` was saved by
  hand meanwhile. Apply refuses when the files changed after its preview and shows the new changes instead.
- **Your own `includeIf` rules** are put back by `gitpersona uninstall` even after many later changes.

### Installing

- **`install.sh`** for macOS and Linux, tested on Apple silicon and Intel Macs and on Linux x86_64 and arm64. It
  never uses `sudo`, refuses a download whose checksum does not match, and changes nothing but the binary and one
  marked `PATH` line in your shell's startup file. `--version`, `--dir` and `--no-modify-path` change that.
- **Release pages** like this one, written for people deciding whether to upgrade, instead of a list of commits.

## Bug fixes

- `install-shell` and the shell checks follow `$ZDOTDIR` for zsh's startup files, as `install.sh` already did.
- GitPersona's own gh queries use the real gh, not its own gh entry, and `doctor` names the real gh.
- The gh entry, the glab entry and the credential helper wait at most 15 seconds instead of hanging.
- `gitpersona ui` no longer leaves a zombie process behind while the page runs.
- The page says when gh could not list your accounts, and `whoami` and `verify` say when Git could not read a
  repository's settings, instead of showing nothing.

## Privacy and security

- **Never stores tokens.** GitHub tokens stay in `gh`; other hosts' tokens stay in your system keychain or Git
  Credential Manager. GitPersona keeps no copy and never prints them.
- **Never reads your keys.** Private key files are only checked to exist; ssh uses them, GitPersona never opens them.
- **Local only.** The web console listens only on 127.0.0.1, behind a link that works once, and stops when its tab is
  closed or after 15 minutes without use. There is no telemetry.
- **Only when you ask.** It connects to the network only to read your accounts' public names and emails during
  setup, and to the SSH hosts when you run `check-ssh` or `verify --ssh`.
- **This release** fixes 46 vulnerabilities in the Go standard library that v0.1.0 (built with Go 1.26.0) contained
  in code GitPersona can reach, mostly in `net/http`, `crypto/tls`, `crypto/x509` and `html/template`
  (GO-2026-4599 to GO-2026-6809; `govulncheck -mode=binary` on a v0.1.0 binary lists them). GitPersona's own code
  and its dependencies had none. The answers cached from gh are kept owner-only in `~/.config/gitpersona/cache/`
  and hold no tokens. Every download carries signed build provenance.

## Install

- Script (macOS and Linux, fully automatic): `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/weikxs/gitpersona/main/install.sh | sh`
- Homebrew (macOS and Linux): `brew install weikxs/tap/gitpersona`, or `brew upgrade gitpersona`
- Go 1.26+: `go install github.com/weikxs/gitpersona/cmd/gitpersona@v0.2.0`
- A package or archive below; check it against `checksums.txt`

| File | Platform |
|---|---|
| `gitpersona_0.2.0_darwin_arm64.tar.gz` | macOS, Apple silicon |
| `gitpersona_0.2.0_darwin_amd64.tar.gz` | macOS, Intel |
| `gitpersona_0.2.0_linux_amd64.deb` / `_arm64.deb` | Debian, Ubuntu (x86_64 / arm64) |
| `gitpersona_0.2.0_linux_amd64.rpm` / `_arm64.rpm` | Fedora, RHEL (x86_64 / arm64) |
| `gitpersona_0.2.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz` / `_arm64.tar.gz` | Any Linux, Alpine and Arch too (x86_64 / arm64) |

Then sign in to each GitHub account once with `gh auth login`, and run `gitpersona setup --web`.

## Compatibility

- macOS 12 or newer on Apple silicon and Intel; Linux on x86_64 and arm64 (glibc or musl: Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora,
  Arch, Alpine and others). Windows is planned.
- Git 2.31 or newer (2.36 or newer if you have your own `includeIf "hasconfig:…"` rules).
- For GitHub profiles, the GitHub CLI 2.40 or newer; for other hosts, a credential helper such as the system keychain
  or Git Credential Manager.
- The web console is in English and Simplified Chinese; the command line is in English.

## Notes

- The macOS binary is not signed or notarized by Apple; Homebrew and the install script remove the quarantine flag.
  By hand: **Open Anyway** in System Settings → Privacy & Security. See
  [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/weikxs/gitpersona/blob/v0.2.0/SECURITY.md#release-binaries-and-macos).
